tossups.text: In this kingdom, a tax was assessed whenever the monarch's beret fell off his head. A civil war in this kingdom resulted when the pretender Pedro Constantino da Silva attempted to usurp the throne. The Prince of Nsoyo was its most powerful noble. This kingdom's main export was raffia cloth, and it fought off an invasion from a neighboring ruler, Queen Nzinga. Joseph Kasa-Vubu attempted to restore this kingdom. This kingdom administered from towns called mbanzas converted to Christianity with the baptism of Nzinga a Mvemba, later known as Afonso I, by Portuguese missionaries. For 10 points, name this kingdom, the namesake of two modern African countries, one of which is led by Joseph Kabila, as well as of Africa's longest river.

If the characteristic of a field does not divide the order of a given finite group, then the group algebra is this type of structure, by Maschke's theorem. In an abelian category, the middle term of a short exact sequence is this type of structure in relation to the other nontrivial terms if and only if there exists a retract of the injection or a section of the surjection. Composition series are useful for modules not nicely expressible as this type of structure, the non-semisimple modules. A group is one of these structures if there exist two subgroups such that every element can be uniquely written as a product of two elements, one from each subgroup. For 10 points, name these structures that are frequently the Cartesian product of substructures with operations defined componentwise.

This instrument's repertoire includes John Stevens's Triumph of the Demon Gods and Alexander Lebedev's Concerto in One Movement. Harvey Phillips was known as the Paganini of this instrument, which plays a solo following a bassoon ostinato at the beginning of Silvestre Revueltas's symphonic poem Sensemaya. Ralph Vaughan Williams composed an F minor concerto for this instrument, which plays the opening melody in Ravel's orchestrated version of Mussorgsky's "Bydlo." In the late 19th century, it replaced the ophicleide in the standard orchestra. The euphonium is pitched one octave higher than this instrument, whose family includes a version of it that wraps around the player, the sousaphone. For 10 points, name this lowest-pitched brass instrument.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for epiglottis function. It plays a key role in the respiratory system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this pharynx-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The pharynx is a key component of the Respiratory system, involved in epiglottis function.

tossups.text: A herdsmen who expelled Portuguese colonists from this modern-day country inspired rulers of its Rozvi empire to take the title Changamire ("chahn-GUH-meer-ay"). The kingdom of Mutapa was founded in this country by its majority Shona ("SHOH-nuh") ethnic group. A flag used by Ian Smith's government prominently featured this modern-day country's national emblem of soapstone birds, which were excavated from an archaeological site here. The name of this modern-day country comes from a "Great" stone city built in the Iron Age. This country's longtime leader Robert Mugabe was born when it was still known as Rhodesia. For 10 points, name this Southeast African country governed from Harare ("huh-RAH-ray").

Arleigh Burke successfully ambushed one of these missions with a destroyer squadron at the Battle of Cape St. George. These missions began shortly after Aritomo Gotō's victory at the Battle of Cape Esperance. The high number of ships sunk in a body travelled by these missions led it it being nicknamed "Ironbottom Sound". The threat of the Cactus Air Force forced these missions to be implemented at night, where ships would sail through "The Slot" and past Savo Island. For ten points, name this system of Japanese convoys which attempted to resupply ground forces on Guadalcanal.

The hydrogenation of alkynes to trans alkenes adds lithium in this substance, which solvates alkali metals' electrons. Wohler added two molar equivalents of this compound to carbon dioxide, disproving vitalism by synthesizing urea. This compound has the highest specific heat of any known substance and is oxidized with a platinum-rhodium catalyst to synthesize nitric acid in the Ostwald Process. This simplest amine has trigonal pyramidal molecular geometry and a lone pair, making it a common Lewis base, and it is synthesized in the Haber process. For 10 points, name this compound with formula NH3.

In a given topological space, if this function becomes arbitrarily small for any combination of inputs past some point in a sequence, then the sequence is Cauchy. The total number of bits at which a string differs gives the Hamming variety of this quantity. The value of p in an Lp space determines how this quantity is calculated. This function must be zero if and only if the inputs are the same. The sum of absolute differences of coordinates gives the "taxicab" variety of this quantity. Three related values of this function must satisfy the triangle inequality, and the norm gives this value for a vector. For 10 points, give this function that tells you how far apart two points are.
acceptableAnswers: accept difference before "Lp" and prompt afterwards

tossups.text: One member of this group, Frank Brandegee, collaborated on a formal statement of this group's views called the Round Robin resolution. Other members of the group included Miles Poindexter and George Moses, who served for some time as American minister to Greece. A better known member of this group had earlier been the head prosecutor of Big Bill Haywood for the murder of Frank Steunenberg, and was known as the "Lion of Idaho." Consisting of 14 Republicans including Hiram Johnson of California, and four Democrats, they notably opposed a clause which required "territorial integrity and existing political independence" to be preserved. Led by William Borah and Henry Cabot Lodge Sr., For 10 points, name this loose collection of politicians who opposed Article X and refused to accept Woodrow Wilson's Treaty of Versailles.

This man argued that Standard Oil had corrupted the Bolivian government, which was the reason for a war between Bolivia and Paraguay. One of this man's books discusses his ambition for running for office in 1936, and includes a list of who this man wanted to have as his cabinet. That book by this man was My First Days in the White House. This man wouldn't get the chance to run, however, as he was assassinated by Carl Weiss in the Louisiana State House, in mid-1935. This man argued for a Universal Basic Income as a part of his "Share Our Wealth" program. For 10 points, the Kingfish was the nickname for what Louisiana Senator who spurred FDR to institute the "2nd New Deal"?

Some Armenian Christians perform a version of this practice called matagh. A ritual that culminated in this practice involved a year of warriors wandering around potentially disputed territory, inviting a king's rivals to challenge them. That ritual ending in this practice was the Vedic Ashvamedha. It doesn't involve herbs, but this practice is essential to the creation of a healing mixture called "omiero." Brigitte Bardot and Manekha Gandhi opposed a festival that prominently features this practice on a large scale; that festival was supposedly ended in 2015 and took place at the Gadhimai Temple in Nepal. The Supreme Court ruled on this practice in a 1993 case involving a Santería church. For 10 points, what religious practice might be carried out by beheading certain things as part of giving offering to the gods?

This function of distance appears in the radial wavefunction for s orbitals. The vapor pressure of a liquid may be approximated by this function of negative one over temperature. When a reaction is said to be "nth-order", the "n" refers to the argument of this function, and a first-order reaction obeys an integrated rate law that contains it. This function's inverse is applied to the reaction quotient in the Nernst equation. This operation, followed by division, is performed on individual concentrations to compute the equilibrium constant using the law of mass action. For 10 points, name this operation which may be applied to a pKa to find the Ka, and which is the inverse of the logarithm.

A musician who used this first name worked with a 64-year-old Elvin Jones on a 1991 album that ends with "Once Upon a Time". That guitarist who used this first name recorded the avant-garde albums Ask the Ages and Black Woman . A musician who used this first name wrote "The Eternal Triangle" for a punningly-titled 1959 album featuring two musicians with this first name alongside Dizzy Gillespie. A musician who used this first name included a version of "Mack the Knife" titled "Moritat" on an album on which Max Roach plays a calypso rhythm on the opening track. A saxophonist who used this first name was inspired by a lullaby his mother sang to him in the Virgin Islands to write the song "St Thomas". For 10 points, what was the first name of the artist of the album Saxophone Colossus , who had the surname Rollins?

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for pancreas digestive enzymes. It plays a key role in the digestive system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this liver-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The liver is a key component of the Digestive system, involved in pancreas digestive enzymes.

tossups.text: In order to take the throne, this ruler killed some relatives but spared his brother Tissa. His son was blinded thanks to the jealousy of his wife and that son later showed up at this man's court with his own son, Samprati. This husband of Tishyaraksha had his name attached to a sculpture of four lions standing back to back now located in the Sarnath Museum. During one war this man won, the Daya River was said to have turned red with blood. This ruler ordered the construction of his namesake pillars inscribed with moral edicts. After the bloody Kalinga War, this man became sickened by death and adopted a more peaceful ideology. For 10 points, name this Mauryan emperor who converted to Buddhism around 260 BC.

A Clint Eastwood biographical film about this musician ends with his death while watching TV with Baroness Nica. It's not Joe Henderson, but this man released a piece referencing his stay in a California state hospital called "Relaxin at Camarillo." One piece by this musician that uses a sequence of ii-V ("two-five") progressions is known as "Blues for Alice." This musician used the chords of Ray Noble's "Cherokee" as inspiration for his "Ko Ko," which, along with "Ornithology," exemplify the fast style of jazz he co-founded with Dizzy Gillespie. For 10 points, name this bebop saxophonist nicknamed "Bird."

According to legend, one of these people drank only half a glass of milk from Pir Budhan Ali Shah, promising that a later generation would drink the rest. The second of these people created a script whose name means "from the mouth of" these people. One of these people created missionaries called masands and appointed female preachers called piris. The Ka'aba legendarily spun around one of these people, who selected his successor after seeing who would pick up his bowl in mud. Five beloved disciples followed each of these people, the last of whom pretended to sacrifice those five and developed the baptism ritual of Amrit Sanchar. The last of these people declared their successor to be the Adi Granth. For 10 points, name these spiritual leaders of Sikhism.

This figure's deeds are recorded by Johnny Inkslinger, who once saved twelve barrels of ink by not crossing his t's or dotting his i's for a week. During the Winter of the Blue Snow, this figure found his most notable companion, for whom he dug the Great Lakes. In another story, this figure created Mount Hood by placing stones on his campfire. For 10 points, name this giant lumberjack whose companion is the blue ox Babe.

Two altered Wollaston prisms are used in one of these devices that are often employed under high magnification and is named for Nomarski. Mirau developed a modification of one of these devices, and a reference is supplied to these devices by the local oscillator. One of these with two parallel plates can be used to observe the Zeeman effect, and another of these devices commonly used for rotation sensing is named for Georges Sagnac. No fringe shift was found in a study that utilized them, thus giving positive evidence for time dilation. They were also used to disprove luminiferous ether theory. For 10 points, name these devices that measure phase differences in light, which were used in the Kennedy-Thorndike and Michelson-Morley experiments.

The Sea Venture sank in Bermuda en route to this colony. William Berkeley's governorship of this colony enraged Nathaniel Bacon, who took a military commission by force from members of this colony's House of Burgesses. It is home to The College of William and Mary and, after becoming a state, its state university was founded by Thomas Jefferson. For 10 points, name this American colony whose capitals were Williamsburg and Jamestown.

parts.text: Name this political party which boasted Victor Berger and Meyer London as its only two members elected to Congress.

In addition to authoring "What's Wrong with New York: A National Problem," this pacifist showed he did not know when to quit, by running as Socialist Party Candidate for President six times, the final time in 1948.
Morris Hillquit derided the Socialist movement in America by using this phrase, a reference to Socialists boasting of the excellence of the namesake public service in Milwaukee.

bonuses.leadin: This end for this party in presidential elections was spelled by the failures of Darlington Hoopes. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this thought experiment which concludes that, if quantum mechanics is complete, measuring part of a quantum system has non-local effects on the rest of the system.

The EPR paradox suggests the existence of local hidden variables in quantum mechanics, but this theorem published in 1964 demonstrates that no local hidden variable theory can account for all quantum mechanical results.

This most famous non-local hidden variable theory is based on de Broglie's pilot-wave theory, and states that particles behave deterministically, treating their eventual measurements as a hidden variable.

bonuses.leadin: It was proposed in a 1935 paper titled, "Can quantum-mechanical description of physical reality be considered complete?" FTPE:

parts.text: Name this musical discipline, the subject of a treatise by Hector Berlioz ("BARELY-ohz") that was revised by Richard Strauss ("RICK-art SHTROWSS").
This Russian composer's Principles of Orchestration uses only examples from his own works, such as Capriccio Espagnol ("kah-PREACH-yoh ay-spahn-YOHL")and Scheherazade ("shuh-HAIR-uh-zahd").

This German-born American composer and professor at Juilliard ("JOO-lee-ard") wrote The Study of Orchestration, which has surpassed Walter Piston's Orchestration as perhaps the most commonly used orchestration textbook.

bonuses.leadin: A 1914 book on this topic by Cecil Forsyth provides a history and description of the Phagotus ("fuh-GOH-tus") of Afranio in its appendix. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with b cells and antibodies.
What is the main function of the T cell in the immune system?
Name another component of the immune system related to b cells and antibodies.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human immune system.

parts.text: The first ugly law was passed in this city in 1867. Joshua Norton declared himself Emperor of the US in this city, where many immigrants were detained in cages at a station on Angel Island.

This city with a de facto ugly law addressed the question of "What, then does the cripple want?" with a 1918 survey. Tom L. Johnson was a highly-praised mayor of this city, which names an 1872 "massacre" in which John Rockefeller bought out his competitors.

Elsewhere in 19th-century American disability history, this inventor of the telephone promoted "oralist" education of the deaf, advocated his father's Visible Speech system, and opposed the use of sign language.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about ugly laws, which made it a crime for the disabled to appear in public in many US cities. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Women householders in this British colony had the right to vote since 1792, although those rights were restricted over time. This West African colony received over 50,000 "recaptives" between 1807 and 1864.
Unlike a larger neighbor, indigenous Maori women were not excluded from this country's pioneering 1893 women's suffrage bill.

Women's suffrage advocates in this country broke the windows of its Parliament in 1912 but weren't granted the technical right to vote until 1947. Women in this country were later said to "hold up half the sky."

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, identify the following about the quest for women's suffrage around the world.

parts.text: Name this phenomenon where a change in current will cause a change in voltage. The rate at which it occurs is measured in henrys.
These devices rely on the mutual form of inductance to operate. Coming in step-up and step-down types, these devices either increase or decrease voltage levels in an electrical circuit.
Ideal transformer models often neglect this form of energy loss, where current flowing through a conductor will release heat. The amount of heat released is proportional to the square of the current.

bonuses.leadin: This phenomenon is a consequence of effects described by Oersted's law and Faraday's law of induction. For 10 points:

parts.text: Name this effect used to explain why acids stronger than hydronium cannot be differentiated by their aqueous ionization. This effect limits the strength of a strong acid by protonating all species.
Per the leveling effect, the basicity of these substances limits the strength of a strong acid. Due to its ability to dissolve many solutes, water is considered a universal one of these substances.

Because they cannot react with the solute, solvents that do [emphasize] not possess this property are unable to limit solute acidity. Ammonia possesses this property, the ability to both donate and accept protons.

bonuses.leadin: This effect explains why nitric and sulfuric acid have roughly equal strengths in dilute aqueous solutions. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this practice of cutting all the hair off one's scalp, often used by the Merovingians to mark pretenders unfit for kingship.
The last Merovingian king, Childeric III, was tonsured after this pope helped overthrow him.
This king, who helped out the Papal States against the Lombards through his namesake "Donation," appealed to Pope Zachary during his overthrow of Childeric III.

bonuses.leadin: Before taking the throne, Dagobert II underwent this punishment. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this revolutionary group that came to power in 1979 under Daniel Ortega.
Before 1979, the Sandinistas sought to organize a revolution in this nation, of which Ortega is again the president as of 2007.

The Sandinistas took over Nicaragua from the last dictator of this longtime ruling family, the younger Anastasio, who had placed Nicaragua under martial law and was reportedly in possession of half of the nation's lands.

bonuses.leadin: In 1990, it was defeated by a coalition of parties known as the National Opposition Union, and Violetta Chamorro became president. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Indian religion, one of whose leaders was Mahavira.
Mahavira was the last of these luminaries of Jainism, who have achieved enlightenment and subsequently show others how to follow, which leads to it being Sanskrit for "Ford-maker".
The last Tirthankara before Mahavira was this man, who established the "fourfold restraint" that would become four of the "great vows" of Jain asceticism.

bonuses.leadin: Their name means "follower of the conquerors" in Sanskrit. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this chemical indicator that's colorless in acidic solutions with a pH less than 8.2 and also turns pink in basic solutions.
Phenolphthalein is commonly applied in this laboratory technique used to determine the concentration of a solution by adding incremental amounts of another known solution.

pH can be derived using this doubly eponymous equation which states that it is the sum of the acid disassociation constant and the logarithm of the concentration of a base over the concentration of its conjugate acid.

bonuses.leadin: It was discovered in 1871 by Adolf von Baeyer, and can be synthesized by the condensation of phthalic anhydride under acidic conditions. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this 2011 Rocksteady game starring Batman, the sequel to a game set at a certain asylum.
Dee Bradley Baker voices this character in Arkham City. This leader of the League of Assassins has built a Lazarus Pit under Wonder Tower, and on film he was portrayed by Liam Neeson.

In a hilariously uncharacteristic role, this man voices The Penguin in Arkham City, complete with terrible British accent. He's better known for voicing every boring video game protagonist ever, such as Desmond Miles in Assassin's Creed and Nathan Drake in Uncharted.

bonuses.leadin: A side quest in this video game involves tracking down the identity killer, Dr. Thomas Elliot, and bosses in this game include Solomon Grundy and Clayface. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with calcitonin.
What is the main function of the thyroid in the endocrine system?
Name another component of the endocrine system related to calcitonin.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human endocrine system.

parts.text: Identify this controversial TV ad that aired only once during an NBC broadcast of the film David and Bathsheba. In it, a girl pulls petals off a flower before a nuclear bomb detonates.
The "Daisy" ad supported this incumbent president's 1964 campaign against Barry Goldwater. This architect of the Great Society became president after the assassination of JFK.

This three-word phrase nicknames a 1953 speech delivered at the UN that proposed creating an International Atomic Energy Agency. This speech also names a program by which the U.S. helped start Iran's nuclear program in 1957.

bonuses.leadin: A voice-over in this ad paraphrases Auden by saying "We must either love each other, or we must die." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this B major song that discusses a 'thick dome of jasmine'. This song is sung primarily in thirds by the maid Mallika and the title character of the opera it appears in.
The "Flower Duet" is part of this composer's opera Lakmé. This French composer also wrote the ballets Coppelia and Sylvia.

This opera by Georges Bizet ("BEE-zay") contains a lyrical "Flower Song" sung by Don José as he professes his love for the title character. The title character of this opera enters with a seductive "Habanera" aria, whilst Escamillo later sings about bullfighting in the "Toreador Song".

bonuses.leadin: This song has been used for British Airways advertising and inflight boarding since the 1980s. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this school of thought, which Popper defined as the logical and necessary development of events according to discernible principles in a 1957 book.
Popper's The Poverty of Historicism was so called in order to allude to The Poverty of Philosophy, an 1847 work by this communist theorist and proponent of historical materialism.
In the title of The Poverty of Philosophy, Marx was himself responding to and critiquing The Philosophy of Poverty, a work by this mutualist French philosopher.

bonuses.leadin: In one work, Karl Popper accused holders of this philosophical idea of having a 'persistent and pernicious influence on the philosophy of society and of politics'. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Medea is the jealous wife of this Greek hero, the leader of the Argonauts.
Medea believed that she earned a place of favor in Jason's life by helping him and his Argonauts recover this mythological relic.
Medea's story was famously told by this Greek playwright, whose other works include Orestes and Electra.

bonuses.leadin: The Greek story of the sorceress Medea has captivated readers for hundreds of generations. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this chunk of DNA that regulates the hydrolysis of a disaccharide to glucose and galactose.
Production of this modified nucleotide by the bacterium activates transcription of the structural genes in the lac operon.
Another enzyme encoded by the lac operon transfers this functional group to beta-galactosides. The removal of this functional group from histone lysine residues results in chromosome condensation.

bonuses.leadin: It includes three genes, including one for a permease, and may be induced by IPTG. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This 1896 case ruled that "separate but equal" was constitutional under the Equal Establishment Clause when the defendant boarded the "whites only" car of a train on the East Louisiana Railroad.
Chief Justice Marshall presided over this 1819 case that determined that Maryland could not attempt to impede the operations of a branch of the Second Bank of the United States by imposing a tax.

This case tested the Fourth Amendment and dealt with police arresting the case's plaintiff for possession of obscene material after failing to find a bombing suspect following a forced entry with a false warrant.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name the following landmark U.S. Supreme Court cases.
